content: Letter 17, Ibn Turka's reply to Amīrzāda Bāysunghur about a treatise of his that a certain individual had objected to (MK's footnote: perhaps Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad Jazarī). He dismisses the objections as empty and ignorant posturing, invites Bāysunghur to have the scholars at his court examine the work thoroughly, saying it rests solely on traditional and rational sources, and calls it a virginal bride from the invisible realm that few are mature enough to marry, i.e., comprehend (TMN/M f. 172a, TMN/MS pp. 12-13, TMN/D pp. 173-75; edition in P.2.1).
